title: 15-16. THE GOD WHO HAS BEEN MY SHEPHERD

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then he blessed Joseph and said, 'May the God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked faithfully, the God who has been my shepherd all my life to this day, the Angel who has delivered me from all harm—may he bless these boys. May they be called by my name and the names of my fathers Abraham and Isaac, and may they increase greatly on the earth.'" — Gen 48:15-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is the first time in Scripture that anyone calls God a shepherd. And it comes from Jacob — a man who spent twenty hard years actually shepherding sheep for a dishonest employer. He knows exactly what the word means. Long nights. Constant watching. Carrying the weak ones. Going out after the lost.

"The God who has been my shepherd all my life to this day."

Think about the life he is describing. Deception, exile, a stolen blessing, a father-in-law who cheated him, a wife buried on a roadside, a daughter violated, a son lost for twenty years. If anyone had reason to say God abandoned him, Jacob did.

And this is his verdict: You have shepherded me all my life. Not "You gave me an easy life," but "You never once left the flock."

David would later take up the same image: The Lord is my shepherd (Ps 23:1). And Jesus would say, "I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep" (Jn 10:11). The Shepherd Jacob leaned on at the end of his life is the one who came in person and died for His sheep.

Look back over your life and ask honestly: has He ever actually left you?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Looking back, where can you see God shepherding you through hard years?
2. What would your one-sentence summary of God's dealings with you be?
3. What does it mean to you that the Shepherd laid down His life?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You have been my shepherd all my life to this day, even in the years I could not see You. Thank You that in Jesus my Shepherd laid down His life for me. Amen.
